## Notes

- The implementation satisfies the core request: `.agent/local/` is ignored, `prepare:local-agent` is added, memory/rubrics are cloned into local context, docs explain the workflow, and tests cover success plus missing rubrics.
- The main rubric-specific gap is rerun behavior when a previously available branch becomes unavailable. The generated context reports the branch as unavailable, but the stale checkout remains on disk and may still be picked up by a local agent.

## Findings

- **WARNING:** Under the idempotency rubric, `refreshCheckout()` only deletes the target checkout after `branchExists()` succeeds. If `agent/rubrics` or `agent/memory` existed during an earlier run and later becomes unavailable or the user points to a missing ref, the function returns an unavailable result without removing the old `.agent/local/rubrics` or `.agent/local/memory` directory. Evidence: early return at [`prepare-agent-context.ts` lines 130-145](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/989b1210de07199be6645dbaea0fe229e0d8e6eb/.agent/src/cli/local/prepare-agent-context.ts#L130-L145), cleanup only on the available path at [lines 147-151](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/989b1210de07199be6645dbaea0fe229e0d8e6eb/.agent/src/cli/local/prepare-agent-context.ts#L147-L151). A focused follow-up test should cover “first clone rubrics, rerun with missing rubrics ref, stale rubrics dir is removed.”

PASS

## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #323 adds local-agent support for the `agent/memory` and `agent/rubrics` branches requested in #121. It creates an ignored `.agent/local/` workspace, adds `prepare:local-agent`, generates `.agent/local/AGENT_CONTEXT.md`, and updates entry docs so local Codex/Claude-style agents can read memory and rubrics before work. This is part of the #314 stacked small-fixes batch and is currently stacked on the #305 branch. The overall design matches the requested shape, but one refresh edge case can leave stale local context behind.

## Review
The reviewers agree the implementation is mostly well-scoped and fits the issue, but two current review artifacts identify a stale-checkout refresh bug. I verified the current PR head still returns before clearing the destination on the missing-branch path.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Stale local context remains when a branch disappears | BLOCKING | `refreshCheckout()` checks branch existence before deleting `.agent/local/<name>`, so a rerun with a missing ref can report unavailable while leaving the prior checkout on disk. |
| Unavailable checkout exports stay in `AGENT_CONTEXT.md` | WARNING | The generated environment block always includes both `MEMORY_DIR` and `RUBRICS_DIR`, even when one checkout is unavailable; the surrounding prose mitigates this, but conditional output would be clearer. |

## Progress
- The core request is implemented: ignored `.agent/local/`, a `prepare:local-agent` script, memory/rubrics clone logic, generated context, docs, and focused tests are present.
- Rubrics review scored the PR as PASS overall but flagged the stale-checkout behavior as an idempotency gap.
- Codex review reproduced the stale-checkout case and treated it as blocking because local agents could consume stale normative rubrics.
- No new inline comment was posted because the stale-checkout finding is already clearly covered in the current PR discussion by the rubrics review comment.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Stale local context remains when a branch disappears</summary>

**Cause:** In [`prepare-agent-context.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/989b1210de07199be6645dbaea0fe229e0d8e6eb/.agent/src/cli/local/prepare-agent-context.ts#L130), the missing-branch path returns before the cleanup at line 147. A previous `.agent/local/rubrics` or `.agent/local/memory` checkout can therefore survive while the generated context says that checkout is unavailable.

**Candidate solutions:** Clear `opts.dir` before returning the missing-branch result, then add a regression test that first creates a checkout, reruns with a missing ref, and asserts the stale directory is removed.

**Comments:** Reviewer severity differed: rubrics review marked this WARNING, while Codex marked it BLOCKING after reproduction. The synthesis treats it as BLOCKING because stale rubrics can mislead local agents on normative guidance.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Unavailable checkout exports stay in `AGENT_CONTEXT.md`</summary>

**Cause:** [`buildAgentContextMarkdown`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/989b1210de07199be6645dbaea0fe229e0d8e6eb/.agent/src/cli/local/prepare-agent-context.ts#L210) emits both export lines unconditionally, while availability is only described in the checkouts and missing-branches sections.

**Candidate solutions:** Emit only available checkout exports, or comment out unavailable exports with an inline unavailable note.

**Comments:** This is advisory. The current text says to set only available variables, so it should not block the branch fix.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: the stale-checkout bug is a concrete branch change with a straightforward automated fix and regression test.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items
- [ ] Clear stale `.agent/local/<name>` directories when the corresponding memory or rubrics branch/ref is unavailable.
- [ ] Add a regression test covering clone-then-rerun-with-missing-ref so stale local context cannot remain.

@sepo-agent /answer 

why this becomes such a huge PR ? anyway to simplify this?

Yes. This PR is huge mostly because of **stacking**, not because the local-agent memory/rubrics change itself is that large.

What happened:

- PR #323 is for #121, but its branch includes earlier stacked commits from the #314 batch:
  - #320: self-approval routing
  - #321: repo config route
  - #322: closed base PR fallback
  - then the actual #121 work
- The actual #121 change is mainly:
  - [`prepare-agent-context.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/323/files#diff-)
  - its focused test
  - `.gitignore`
  - `AGENT.md`
  - a few docs
- Measured by commits, the actual #121 work is about **8 files / ~573 additions**, while the PR currently shows **49 files / ~3k additions** because GitHub is displaying the stacked base too.

Best simplification options:

1. **Cleanest:** recreate/rebase #323 from current `main` and cherry-pick only the two #121 commits:
   - `989b1210` Prepare local agent memory and rubrics context
   - `3f32e1f` Clear stale local context on missing refs

   That should reduce the PR to the real local-agent scope.

2. **If we intentionally want a stack:** retarget #323’s base to the previous stack PR branch, then merge the stack in order. But since #322 is already merged and #121 looks mostly independent, I think a fresh branch from `main` is better here.

3. **Optional code-scope reduction:** keep only the CLI, test, `.gitignore`, `AGENT.md`, and one install/local-agent doc in this PR. The extra architecture docs can be follow-up if we want an even smaller first pass.

My recommendation: **replace/rebase this PR onto current `main` with only the #121 commits**. The implementation itself is reasonable; the PR presentation is the problem.
